**<mark>ICSG PRESS RELEASE Date Issued: 21</mark>**<sup>**st**</sup> **<mark>July 2010</mark>** 



# **Copper: Preliminary Data for April 2010** 

The International Copper Study Group (ICSG) released preliminary data for April 2010 world copper supply and demand in its July 2010 Copper Bulletin. The Bulletin is available for sale upon request. 

According to preliminary ICSG data, the refined copper market balance for April 2010 indicated a market deficit of 60,000 metric tonnes. When making seasonal adjustments for world refined production and usage, April showed a surplus of about 30,000 t. The apparent refined copper balance for the first four months of 2010, including revisions to data previously presented, indicates a production deficit of 67,000 t (a seasonally adjusted surplus of 119,000 t). This compares with a production surplus of around 75,000 t (a seasonally adjusted surplus of about 245,000 t) for the same period in 2009. 

World refined copper usage in April 2010 grew by 5.8% compared with that in April 2009, mainly owing to the continued recovery of usage in Japan, the European Union (EU) and the United States.  Chinese apparent usage remained unchanged from the high level of April 2009. During the first four months of 2010, world usage grew by 8.3%compared with that in the first 4 months of 2009:  Usage grew by 3% in China, 11% in the EU, 43% in Japan and 2.7% in the United States.  Combined, these four regions currently account for 71% of total world refined copper usage. 

World mine production in the first four months of 2010 grew by 1.4% (70,000 t) compared with that in the same period of 2009, yet remained about 6.8% below that for the last 4 months of 2009.  Compared with that in the first 4 months of 2009, concentrate production grew by 1.3% while solvent extraction-electrowinning (SX-EW) grew by 2%. Production in Chile was up slightly (3.7%) from its low level during the first 4 months of 2009, but output from other major producers such as Peru, the United States, Australia and Indonesia decreased by an aggregated 7.5%.  These four countries represent around 25% of total world copper mine production. Mine production capacity utilization rates in the first 4 months of 2010 were around 78%. 

During the first four months of 2010, world refined production increased by 5.8% (340,000 t) compared with production in the same period of 2009: primary production increased by 2.1%, while secondary production (from scrap) increased by 28%. Note that the large relative increase in secondary refined copper production reflects in part the lower copper prices and consequent tight scrap market that existed in early 2009. Refined production increased by 34% in Africa, 11% in Asia and 8% in Europe, but decreased in the Americas by 2.4% and in Oceania by 28%. The refined production capacity utilization rate in the first four months of 2010 increased to almost 80% from 77% in the same period of 2009 and reflects increased scrap availability a

nd the restoration of temporary cuts made in early 2009. The average LME cash price for June 2010 was US$ 6,499.30 per tonne, down from the May 2010 average of US$ 6,837.68 per tonne. The 2010 high and low copper prices through the end of May were US$7,950.50 and US$6,091.00 per tonne, respectively, and the average was US$7,130.13 per tonne. As of the end of June 2010, copper stocks held at the major metal exchanges (LME, COMEX, SHFE) totalled 666,448 t, a decrease of 21,243 t from stocks held at the end of December 2009.
